clue.text: Drop round, breaking engagement, being wretched

indicators.note: something breaking into a thing splits it open and sits inside it

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting or appointment

indicators.note: to turn something round is to face it the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to drop something is to lose it

explanation.surface: Someone drops a round of drinks, breaks off an engagement, and feels miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop round' reads like a casual visit, but 'Drop' is a verb on its own and 'round' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate and wretched are synonyms for being utterly miserable and forlorn.

clue.text: Liability in first performance, not united

indicators.note: 'not' tells the solver to leave out the letter that follows it

parts.note: a debut is someone's first public appearance
U is the standard abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A financial burden arising from an opening show that lacked unity.
explanation.walkthrough: Take U out of DEBUT to leave DEBT.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money owed, which is a liability on any balance sheet.

clue.text: Clarity from head of state, quietly in control

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of state

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to harness something is to control and use it
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A leader's clarity comes from quietly staying in control.
explanation.walkthrough: p comes from the musical marking piano, which tells players to play softly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpness of an image or idea is its clarity or crispness of focus.

clue.text: Nothing upset firm line followed by new president

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
Co is the abbreviation for company
L is a standard abbreviation for line
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A company's bottom line goes unexpectedly before a new president takes office.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth president of the United States.

clue.text: Moving of earth around uneven road

indicators.note: letters placed around another piece enclose it
moving the letters around shifts them into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written, to be rearranged
an uneven surface is rough

explanation.surface: Earthmovers are working around a bumpy road surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving of earth' sounds like excavation, but 'of' joins the fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a main road or public street open at both ends for traffic.

clue.text: Some aghast at usurper's position

indicators.note: 'some' points to just a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of aghast, all of at, and the start of usurper's

explanation.surface: Some people are horrified at the position a usurper has seized.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or rank, that is, a position in society.

clue.text: Employees without leader going over odd bits of extra material

indicators.note: a word without its leader loses its opening letter

parts.note: a firm's employees are its staff

indicators.note: odd bits are the letters in the first, third and fifth positions

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of extra

explanation.surface: Workers with no boss are looking over scraps of spare fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'going over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven fabric, often silk, used for dresses.

clue.text: Observance after time lacking originality

indicators.note: 'after' sends the observance second, behind the time abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a rite is a ceremonial observance

explanation.surface: A ritual repeated over and over becomes stale.
explanation.walkthrough: The observance comes after time, so T leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite remarks are hackneyed and overused, so they show no originality.

clue.text: Doctor grew silent, getting uncomfortably hot

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A physician falls quiet as the room becomes stifling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweltering describes oppressive heat that makes a person sweat and feel uncomfortable.

clue.text: Clever type getting support with folder for incoming messages

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
the inbox is where new emails arrive

explanation.surface: A bright spark sets up support and an email inbox.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAINBOX is informal British slang for a very clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainbox is a colloquial term for a highly intelligent person.

clue.text: Duty abandoned, freeze

parts.note: an abandoned event is called off
to freeze something is to ice it

explanation.surface: Someone walks away from their responsibilities, leaving them frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a position of duty or a task one is charged with, as in 'the office of mayor'.

clue.text: Detective wearing singlet on air got rattled

parts.note: someone dressed in a garment is wearing it

indicators.note: rattled letters have been shaken up into disorder

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
the letters as written

explanation.surface: A detective in a vest appears on the airwaves and gets flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a vest is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: An investigator looks into crimes, which is what a detective does.

clue.text: Declaration in part of speech with substance that's binding

parts.note: a pronoun is one of the parts of speech
cement binds building materials together

explanation.surface: A grammarian's binding statement about a word class.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronouncement is a formal statement or official declaration.

clue.text: Stirring up old men — me, George Sand?

indicators.note: stirring mixes things together, so the letters end up in a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A provocative woman boasts of stirring up old men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like part of 'stirring up', but its letters are fodder. George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin.
explanation.definitionFit: George Sand is an example of a pseudonym used by an author, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Area of water in middle of land behind old church

indicators.note: 'behind' sends the land piece second, after the old church

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: the two central letters of land

explanation.surface: A lake sits inland behind an old church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' puts the land piece after O and CE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast expanse of sea water covering much of the globe.

clue.text: Soldier deployed near ridge

indicators.note: deployed troops are spread out and rearranged, as these letters are

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A soldier is posted near a mountain ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is an infantry soldier, originally one who threw grenades.

clue.text: One working under Conservative in incompetent establishment

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: inept means incompetent
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
I is the Roman numeral one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An employee toils for a Tory boss in a badly run firm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts I and ON below the INEPT and C piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Inception and establishment both mean the founding or beginning of something.

clue.text: Embarrass party minute before match

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
M is the abbreviation for minute
to fit is to match or suit

explanation.surface: Someone is embarrassed at a party just before a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit someone is to make them feel uneasy or embarrassed.

clue.text: Unknown book penned by sailor? Correct

indicators.note: something penned by another is shut inside it, as in a pen

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman
B is the abbreviation for book
to cure a fault is to correct it

explanation.surface: An unknown book written by a sailor, the clue wonders, and then confirms it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like 'written', but it means B is placed inside OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means little known, so an obscure figure is largely unknown.

clue.text: Nut about to enter enclosure

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
ca (circa) means about

explanation.surface: A nut is about to be dropped into a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecan is the edible nut of a North American hickory tree.

clue.text: Complaint from annoying person full of rubbish

indicators.note: something full of another holds it inside

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person
rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by a tiresome person who talks nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is a formal objection, which is a kind of complaint.

clue.text: Campaigning body urges proper reforms, holding us back

indicators.note: going back means reading in the opposite direction
one piece holding another keeps it inside
to reform something is to reshape it, so these letters take a new form

parts.note: the letters as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lobby group pushes for proper reform while holding the nation back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reforms' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb that rearranges the letters around the reversed US.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressure group is an organisation that campaigns to influence public policy.

clue.text: Be second in departure

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: an exit is a departure
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An instruction to come second as people leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, to have being or life.

clue.text: Joint work's ending most of poverty

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter
the ending of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of work
need is want or poverty

explanation.surface: A shared job comes to an end, leaving most people poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint work' reads as a collaboration; 'Joint' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint between the thigh and the lower leg.

clue.text: Single leprechaun I question partially

indicators.note: partially means only a part of the preceding words is used

parts.note: the letters run from the end of leprechaun through I to the start of question

explanation.surface: Someone questions a lone leprechaun.
explanation.definitionFit: Unique means being the only one of its kind, that is, single.

clue.text: Area with unusual heat in north of capital city

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: unusual letters are out of their normal order

parts.note: the letters as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A region with strange heat in the north of a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but its letters join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Athenian is the adjective for Athens, the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Revolutionary encounters English judge

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word reads the other way

parts.note: to encounter someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: A rebel comes face to face with an English magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to consider or regard.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem something is to consider or deem it, as in 'I esteem it an honour'.

clue.text: Retired, overwhelmed by change? That's affectation

indicators.note: something overwhelmed by another is swallowed up and enclosed

parts.note: loose change is pennies, or pence
ret. is the abbreviation for retired

explanation.surface: A retiree swamped by change dismisses it all as showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: Pence are British pennies, the small coins of loose change.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a false show or display, which is what an affectation is.
